title: Inaugural council meeting moved; outgoing councillors honoured
subtitle: Farewell tributes to two departing councillors, Cowan Recreation Centre opening, and Remembrance Day ceremony details
overview: Council held a short special meeting on November 6. Its one substantive decision was to move the Inaugural Council Meeting for the 2026-2030 term from November 16 to November 23, 2026 {{vote:m1}}. This sets the date when the new council will begin its term.

Most of the meeting was spent recognizing two outgoing members of Council: Councillor A. Owodunni, who served from 2022 to 2026, and Councillor S. Stretch, who served from 2024 to 2026. Each received a token of appreciation and tribute videos from colleagues. The Mayor also thanked senior staff, the Clerk's team and the Office of Mayor and Council team for their work during the term.

The Mayor reminded residents that the new Cowan Recreation Centre opens on Saturday, November 14, with activities through the following week. Details are on the City website. A Remembrance Day ceremony is set for November 11 at the Cenotaph at Duke and Frederick Streets, beginning at 10:30 a.m. Council also gave final reading to by-laws and confirmed its proceedings before adjourning.

decisions.detail: Council amended the 2026 Council and Committee Schedule to move the Inaugural Council Meeting for the 2026-2030 term from November 16 to November 23, 2026.

debate: There was no discussion on the schedule change; the Mayor asked for debate, none was offered, and the motion was put to a vote.
The rest of the meeting was tribute rather than debate. Speakers praised the two outgoing councillors' work on community facilities, housing, downtown safety and newcomer inclusion.

In reflections, one outgoing councillor described council decisions as involving many shades of grey rather than clear-cut choices. The other credited colleagues with teaching the value of listening to residents and engaging the community.
